system.name: Prism
system.one_liner: a GPU-disaggregated serving system for deep learning recommendation models that splits inference into CPU-intensive and GPU-efficient subgraphs across disaggregated nodes

components.name: ① Existing software stack
components.role: baseline: the full software stack and combined CPU/GPU/NPU hardware co-located on one server, no disaggregation

components.name: ② Graph-level disaggregation
components.role: splits above the framework: Models/Framework stay local while API/Driver/Hardware move to a Remote Server, linked by RDMA between the two framework instances

components.name: ③ API-level disaggregation
components.role: splits at the device API: a local API (rCUDA) Client forwards calls over RDMA to a remote API (rCUDA) Server that owns the Driver and Hardware layers

components.name: ④ Hardware-level disaggregation
components.role: keeps the entire software stack local and moves only the GPU/NPU hardware to a Remote Server over a PCIe/CXL Switch

components.name: Models
components.role: application-layer model code, present on the Local (or single) Server in every panel

components.name: TensorFlow/PyTorch
components.role: ML framework layer; in Graph-level disaggregation it also runs on the Remote Server and talks to the local instance over RDMA

components.name: Device SDK (CUDA)
components.role: vendor device API layer; relocated to the Remote Server in Graph-level disaggregation

components.name: Device Runtime
components.role: runtime layer beneath the device SDK, shown only in the API-level disaggregation stack

components.name: API (rCUDA) Client
components.role: intercepts device API calls locally and forwards them to the remote API server

components.name: API (rCUDA) Server
components.role: receives forwarded API calls and executes them against the local Driver/Hardware

components.name: PCIe Driver
components.role: low-level PCIe bus driver layer beneath the device driver

components.name: CPU
components.role: host processor hardware; stays on the Local Server in every disaggregated configuration shown

components.name: GPU/NPU
components.role: accelerator hardware; combined with the CPU in the non-disaggregated baseline, and the only layer relocated in Hardware-level disaggregation

content.key_idea: GPU disaggregation can cut the stack at different layers (framework, device API/rCUDA, or raw hardware over PCIe/CXL), each moving a different boundary between what stays local and what runs remotely.
content.reading_order: Each of the four labeled panels top-to-bottom as a layered stack split into Local/Remote Server columns, comparing where the network link (RDMA or PCIe/CXL) cuts the stack.

evidence: Figure 5: GPU disaggregation at different levels.

summary: This background figure surveys four ways to physically disaggregate GPUs from a server's CPU, reusing the same layered software-stack diagram (Application/Models, Framework/TensorFlow-PyTorch, API/Device SDK, Driver, Hardware) split into Local/Remote Server columns. Panel 1 shows the existing, non-disaggregated stack with every layer and a combined CPU/GPU/NPU on one server. Panel 2, graph-level disaggregation, keeps Models and the framework local while the framework's remote counterpart, API, driver, and hardware sit on a remote server, linked by RDMA between the two framework instances. Panel 3, API-level disaggregation, keeps everything down to an API (rCUDA) Client local and forwards calls over RDMA to a remote API (rCUDA) Server owning the driver and hardware. Panel 4, hardware-level disaggregation, keeps the whole software stack local and moves only the GPU/NPU across a PCIe/CXL switch. Consistent per-layer colors make the relocated boundary easy to compare across panels.
